title: VIP ICR Intake and Prioritization Matrix: Impact-Confidence-Risk for Top-Account Escalations
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Executive and strategic customers frequently submit high-stakes roadmap requests and escalations that bypass standard intake lanes. Current ad-hoc prioritization leads to reactive engineering work, missed SLAs for high-touch customers, and inconsistent communication across Sales, CS, and Product.

Objective: Create a repeatable VIP intake and prioritization matrix (ICR = Impact, Confidence, Risk) that quantifies requests from top accounts, generates recommended SLA lanes (Fast-Track / Standard / Watchlist), and produces a one-page decision artifact for leadership and Sales negotiation. The matrix should be lightweight, defensible, and integrable into the existing intake form and roadmap cadence.

Scope:
- Design the ICR scoring rubric and thresholds for SLA lanes.
- Implement a companion intake form in Confluence/Sheets used by AMs and CS to submit VIP asks.
- Integrate recommendations into the Product intake dashboard (read-only view for Sales).
- Define runbook for escalation handling, stakeholders, and expected comm windows.
- Pilot with three strategic accounts, then iterate before broader rollout.
acceptance_criteria: ICR rubric published in Confluence with examples and scoring guide
Intake form prototype available and collects required fields (business impact, affected customers, reproducible steps, timeline, legal/compliance flags)
Automated recommendation (Fast-Track / Standard / Watchlist) displayed in the intake dashboard based on ICR score
SLA lane definitions with owner, expected response time, and escalation path documented
Pilot with 3 accounts completed and feedback captured; at least 2/3 report improved clarity on timelines
Playbook approved by Head of Product and Sales leadership
implementation_steps: 1) Workshop with Sales/CS/Eng to align on impact and confidence definitions (Jan 20)
2) Draft rubric and runbook; iterate with PM and GTM (Jan 27)
3) Build intake form (Confluence + Google Sheet) and wire read-only view in Product dashboard (Feb 3)
4) Pilot intake with 3 assigned accounts (Feb 10 - Feb 28)
5) Collect metrics and decision logs; adjust thresholds and communication templates (Mar 3)
6) Finalize playbook and train AMs/CS; prepare rollout plan (Mar 7)
7) Hand-off to PMO for operationalization into next cadence (Mar 14)
metrics_and_kpis: Mean time to acknowledged response for VIP requests (target < 48h)
Percent of VIP requests assigned to a lane with an owner (target 100%)
Percent of pilot requests meeting published ETA (target >= 80%)
Number of downstream firefights reduced (tracked qualitatively in weekly review)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales may attempt to game scores to fast-track requests -> Mitigation: include confidence checks, require quantifiable evidence and AM manager sign-off
Risk: Engineering capacity limited for Fast-Track -> Mitigation: define capacity guardrail and automatic fallback to Standard with communication template
Risk: Overhead for intake reduces adoption -> Mitigation: keep form minimal; build one-click promotion from existing support case or customer brief
Risk: Conflicting ownership between Sales and CS -> Mitigation: explicit owners in runbook and monthly SLT review of top 10 active VIP requests
